Confidently GF choices are the organic smoothies, organic coffee and mugwort tea; the curry, burrito (wheat tortilla) and 21-grain sandwich are wheat or unverified. Wheat bread/burritos share the kitchen, and seasoned side dishes likely use ordinary (wheat) soy sauce — no tamari mentioned. A celiac should confirm each dish with staff and not assume the curry roux is safe.

chef_bio.background: Owner Masayuki Kamimae studied dance in California, where organic food was part of his everyday life. Returning to Japan he found organic products hard to access and felt his health suffer from increased food additives, which motivated him to open ONE EARTH so future generations could eat well. He designed the basement space himself, marked by a green sign, in the Mikawa-cho / Namiki-dori area of central Hiroshima. The shop pairs the ONE EARTH organic cafe with the lovefamcook plant-based kitchen.
chef_bio.philosophy: 口から食べるもので未来を考える — thinking about Japan's future through what we put in our mouths, extending the healthy lifespan of children and adults alike through organic, additive-free food.
chef_bio.specialty: Organic additive-free plant-forward cafe fare — moringa/vegan curry, acai bowls, organic smoothies

anecdotes.text: Kamimae says he does not want organic treated as something special, but wants customers to embrace it with familiarity in daily life.
His time studying dance in California, where he ate organic routinely, is the origin story for founding the cafe after returning to an additive-heavy diet in Japan.

hiro_undo_komeko_udon.gf_detail: A rice-flour udon noodle shop and micro-factory where the noodles are 100% domestic rice flour and the whole menu is built to be wheat-free. The shop states 「小麦粉不使用」 (no wheat flour used) and 「出汁やタレなどもすべてグルテンフリー」 (the dashi, sauces and everything are all gluten-free), which makes it one of the rare celiac-safe SAVORY sit-down meals in central Hiroshima. Because the venue is a dedicated 米粉 (rice-flour) noodle operation rather than a mixed wheat kitchen, cross-contact risk is low, but the shop has not published a formal dedicated-fryer / allergen-protocol statement, so a celiac diner should still confirm at the counter that their bowl shares no equipment with any wheat item and that soy-based tare is the GF one.
hiro_undo_komeko_udon.vegan_detail: The parent okonomiyaki brand undo opened this factory partly in response to repeated vegan and gluten-free requests from foreign tourists, and offers vegan options (e.g. a vegetable okonomiyaki using rice-flour noodles/rice paper, ~¥1,200). Not every udon is vegan (mentaiko-mayo and some dashi contain fish/animal products), so vegans should confirm which broth and toppings are plant-based.

gf_review.why: This is a wheat-inherent cuisine (udon) at a positive tier, so I presumed it wrong and went hunting for the wheat: I found instead that the noodles are documented 100% rice flour with 「小麦粉不使用」, that the shop states 「出汁やタレなどもすべてグルテンフリー」 (broth AND tare — the usual trap), and, critically, that the sister wheat okonomiyaki shop 広島お好み焼き undo sits in a SEPARATE building across the street rather than sharing a kitchen. Corroboration is genuinely independent and includes celiac-grade evidence: FindMeGlutenFree lists undo factory as a dedicated gluten-free restaurant with celiac reviewers calling it the 'best gf udon i've ever had', alongside a Hiroshima Home TV news segment and a separate on-site interview by bm-peekaboo. I found no glutening report, no closure notice, and no wheat item on the menu. Remaining gaps: no written allergen protocol, and shared boiling water within the shop is undocumented.
red_flags: VITAL WHEAT GLUTEN LOOPHOLE: 「小麦粉不使用」 (no wheat FLOUR) does not exclude 小麦グルテン/小麦たんぱく, which Hiroshima rice-flour producers commonly add for chew — and rice-flour udon is exactly where that additive is used. Partly offset by the shop's separate blanket 「すべてグルテンフリー」 claim and by celiac reviewers eating there without incident, but ask about 小麦グルテン by name at the counter
No written allergen/cross-contact protocol published by the shop

Sister shop 広島お好み焼き undo (wheat okonomiyaki) is across the street under the same brand — do not walk into the wrong door; the GF okonomiyaki served there is cooked on a teppan that also cooks wheat batter
Address discrepancy: shop and press give 中区大手町1-5-18 IBAビル 1F, FindMeGlutenFree lists 大手町1-7-21 — confirm before travelling

hiro_yamaichi_bekkan.gf_detail: [Held at "ask" 2026-08-20] The description below was not traceable to any source, so the GF label is held down until it is. A kappo-style kaiseki ryokan right by the Miyajima ferry terminal that will convert its multi-course meals to gluten-free ON REQUEST. Its own site states 「可能な限り、全てのお料理をグルテンフリー仕様に変更できます。また、各種アレルギー対応のお食事も可能ですので、事前にお電話にて詳細をお知らせくださいませ」— i.e. as far as possible all dishes can be remade gluten-free, and various allergies accommodated, but you MUST phone in advance. Because this is a shared ryokan kitchen (wheat soy sauce, tempura, wheat-thickened sauces are all normally present) rather than a dedicated GF facility, this caps at 'options': the conversion depends on advance notice and careful kitchen handling, so a celiac should call, explain celiac disease (セリアック病／小麦アレルギー), and confirm cross-contact precautions.
hiro_yamaichi_bekkan.vegan_detail: Offers a fully plant-based vegetarian/vegan kaiseki course in which vegetables are styled to resemble meat and fish, with even the seasonings kept animal-free; the venue explicitly markets to vegetarian, vegan and halal-conscious guests. Groups can mix — some diners take the vegan course while others eat the standard meal. Arrange in advance so the plant-based course can be prepared.

High value because GF-friendly options on the island itself are scarce — most day-trippers have to eat back in Miyajimaguchi or Hiroshima city.

It presents itself as a place to share Japan's culinary excellence with international guests, actively catering to vegetarian, vegan, halal-conscious and gluten-free diners. The kitchen develops plant-based kaiseki in which vegetables are shaped to look like meat and fish, and offers to convert standard courses to gluten-free as much as possible on advance request.

cultural_comfort.note: A counter stall inside Okonomimura; no stated English-specific accommodation found for this stall individually.

hiro_teppan_niichi.gf_detail: A standard-build Hiroshima okonomiyaki shop; the noodle is wheat and is cooked in a dashi broth rather than plain, but the wheat itself is unchanged. No gluten-free adaptation documented.
hiro_teppan_niichi.vegan_detail: The signature noodle broth is fish-powder (umami) based; no vegan build documented.
hiro_teppan_niichi.notes: [Mom & Pop · okonomiyaki] Opened December 21, 2025 near Shin-Inokuchi Station by an owner from the local Inokuchi area, explicitly framed around community pride and revitalizing the neighborhood. Signature technique: the noodle is cooked in a fish-powder (umami) dashi broth rather than pan-fried plain -- a real, describable noodle-cooking deviation, alongside a stated emphasis on steaming the cabbage to bring out its own sweetness before it's baked into the stack.

chef_bio.background: Owner is originally from the Inokuchi neighborhood and previously worked at Otafuku Sauce -- Hiroshima okonomiyaki's best-known sauce maker -- before opening this shop in December 2025 with the explicit goal of giving the local area a gathering place and a source of neighborhood pride.
chef_bio.philosophy: States a deliberate focus on steaming the cabbage to draw out its natural sweetness before the stack is finished, and on cooking the noodle in a dashi broth carrying fish-powder umami rather than frying it plain.

anecdotes.text: The owner previously worked at Otafuku Sauce -- the company most associated with Hiroshima okonomiyaki sauce itself -- before opening this shop in his home neighborhood of Inokuchi, an industry-insider background distinct from the more common "trained at another okonomiyaki shop" lineage story found elsewhere in this dataset.
Signature technique cooks the noodle in a broth carrying fish-powder umami, rather than pan-frying it plain as most shops do -- described as "出汁で焼く麺" (noodle cooked in dashi).

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: The shop's own site and local coverage (hiroshima-okonomiyaki.com's "maioko" review series) describe Teppan Niichi as a December 2025 opening by an Inokuchi-native owner and former Otafuku Sauce employee, built around neighborhood revitalization. Signature is a noodle cooked in a fish-powder dashi broth rather than pan-fried plain, alongside deliberate cabbage-steaming for sweetness.

cultural_comfort.note: A new, small neighborhood shop; no stated English-language accommodation found.

gf_cross_contamination.text: Noodle is wheat, cooked in a dashi broth rather than fried plain, but remains wheat; no gluten-free adaptation documented.

vegan_cross_contact.text: Signature noodle broth is fish-powder based; not vegan.
